an4.62:1.1: Then Anāthapiṇḍika the householder went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, having bowed down to the Blessed One, sat to one side.
an4.62:2.1: As he was sitting there, the Blessed One said to him, “Householder, there are these four types of bliss that—depending on time & occasion—can be experienced by a householder partaking of sensuality.
an4.62:2.3: The bliss of having, the bliss of partaking, the bliss of debtlessness, & the bliss of blamelessness.
an4.62:3.1: “And which is the bliss of having?
an4.62:3.2: There is the case where a son of a good family has wealth earned through his efforts & enterprise, amassed through the strength of his arms and piled up through the sweat of his brow, righteous wealth righteously gained.
an4.62:3.3: [Thinking,] ‘I have wealth earned through my efforts & enterprise, amassed through the strength of my arms and piled up through the sweat of my brow, righteous wealth righteously gained,’ he experiences bliss, experiences joy.
an4.62:3.4: This is called the bliss of having.
an4.62:4.1: “And which is the bliss of partaking?
an4.62:4.2: There is the case where a son of a good family, using the wealth earned through his efforts & enterprise, amassed through the strength of his arms and piled up through the sweat of his brow—righteous wealth righteously gained—partakes of his wealth & makes merit.
an4.62:4.3: [Thinking,] ‘Using the wealth earned through my efforts & enterprise, amassed through the strength of my arms and piled up through the sweat of my brow—righteous wealth righteously gained—I partake of my wealth & make merit,’ he experiences bliss, experiences joy.
an4.62:4.4: This is called the bliss of partaking.
an4.62:5.1: “And which is the bliss of debtlessness?
an4.62:5.2: There is the case where a son of a good family owes nothing—large or small—to anyone at all.
an4.62:5.3: [Thinking,] ‘I owe nothing—large or small—to anyone at all,’ he experiences bliss, experiences joy.
an4.62:5.4: This is called the bliss of debtlessness.
an4.62:6.1: “And which is the bliss of blamelessness?
an4.62:6.2: There is the case where the disciple of the noble ones is endowed with blameless bodily action, blameless verbal action, blameless mental action.
an4.62:6.3: [Thinking,] ‘I am endowed with blameless bodily action, blameless verbal action, blameless mental action,’ he experiences bliss, experiences joy.
an4.62:6.4: This is called the bliss of blamelessness.
an4.62:6.5: “Householder, these are four types of bliss that—depending on time & occasion—can be experienced by a householder partaking of sensuality.”

an4.62:7.4: a mortal then sees clearly with discernment.
